## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-10-cell-cell-communication-analysis-using-nichenet/>

Part 1 of 2. NicheNet asks which ligands, produced by *sender* cells, best
explain the gene expression changes seen in a *receiver* cell type. It combines
prior knowledge (a ligand-receptor network, a ligand-target regulatory
potential matrix and signaling networks) with the expressed genes of the
data set. Here the receiver is `params$receiver` (CD4+ T cells in the article),
the gene set of interest is the set of genes upregulated in
`params$condition.oi` versus `params$condition.reference` in the receiver, and
the senders are all other cell types.

This notebook: downloads (and caches) the human NicheNet prior models, loads
the downsampled annotated Seurat object, defines receiver and sender cells,
finds the expressed genes, defines the DE gene set of interest, defines the
potential ligands (sender-agnostic and sender-focused) and ranks them by ligand
activity. It ends by saving the objects needed by part 2 (visualization,
receptors, sender assignment, optional extended prioritization, signaling paths
and the circos plot).

**Input:** the downsampled Seurat object written by tutorial 7 part 1
(`scRNAseq_tutorial_7_trajectory_monocle3/tut7_trajectory_monocle3_part1.Rmd`).
That notebook must be run first to create `seurat_subset_downsampled.rds`; no
downsampling is done here.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (installation, download and
steps 1-7; the install block is in `tut10_R_requirements.R`). Changes made for
this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter, paths
built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or `FIX:`
in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load Libraries, Prior Models, and Data
#-----------------------------------------------
library(nichenetr)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(patchwork)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_10_cell_communication_nichenet/tut10_cell_communication_nichenet_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Working directories
base.dir <- params$base.dir
nichenet.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$nichenet.subdir)

# Create output directories
# (article: dir.create("plots/nichenet", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))
for (d in c("plots/nichenet", "results")) {
  dir.create(file.path(nichenet.dir, d), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

# Cache folder for the prior models (shared between parts and re-runs)
model.cache.dir <- if (nzchar(params$model.cache.dir)) path.expand(params$model.cache.dir) else file.path(base.dir, "nichenet_models")
dir.create(model.cache.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col

cat("Environment setup complete!\n")
cat("Seurat version:", as.character(packageVersion("Seurat")), "\n")
cat("nichenetr version:", as.character(packageVersion("nichenetr")), "\n")
```

## Downloading the NicheNet prior model files

The four prior model files are downloaded once and cached; files already in the
cache folder are not downloaded again.

```{r download_priors}
# Recommended: download once and save locally to avoid repeated downloads
options(timeout = params$download.timeout)  # increase timeout for large files

# ADDED: the four article download.file() calls as one loop over parallel
# param lists, each guarded by file.exists() and writing into the cache folder.
# (The article notes the last file, ligand_tf_matrix, is required for the
# signaling path inference only - Step 13 here, "Step 14" in the article.)
stopifnot(length(params$model.files) == length(params$model.local.names))
for (i in seq_along(params$model.files)) {
  dest <- file.path(model.cache.dir, params$model.local.names[[i]])
  if (file.exists(dest)) {
    cat("Already downloaded:", dest, "\n")
  } else {
    download.file(
      url = paste0(params$zenodo.base, params$model.files[[i]]),
      destfile = dest
    )
  }
}
```

## Load prior models and data

```{r step1b_load_models_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1 (continued): Load prior models and data
#-----------------------------------------------

# Load NicheNet prior model files (downloaded earlier)
lr_network           <- readRDS(file.path(model.cache.dir, "lr_network_human.rds"))
ligand_target_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(model.cache.dir, "ligand_target_matrix_human.rds"))
weighted_networks    <- readRDS(file.path(model.cache.dir, "weighted_networks_human.rds"))

# Keep only unique ligand-receptor pairs
lr_network <- lr_network %>% distinct(from, to)

# Load the downsampled annotated Seurat object
# (ADDED: from tutorial 7 part 1, which must have been run first)
input.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$input.subdir, params$input.rds)
stopifnot(file.exists(input.file))
cat("Reading in Seurat object:", input.file, "\n")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(input.file)

# ADDED: check the metadata columns, assay and counts layer that are needed
stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, condition.col) %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))
stopifnot(params$assay %in% names(seurat_obj@assays))
if (inherits(seurat_obj[[params$assay]], "Assay5") &&
    !"counts" %in% Layers(seurat_obj[[params$assay]])) {
  # split layers (counts.1, counts.2, ...) need to be joined for GetAssayData()
  seurat_obj <- JoinLayers(seurat_obj, assay = params$assay)
}

# Set cell type labels as the active identity for NicheNet
# (article: Idents(seurat_obj) <- seurat_obj$final_annotation)
Idents(seurat_obj) <- seurat_obj[[celltype.col, drop = TRUE]]

# Verify cell types and conditions
# (ADDED: print() so the tables show in the rendered notebook)
print(table(seurat_obj[[celltype.col, drop = TRUE]]))
print(table(seurat_obj[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]]))
```

## Define receiver and sender cell types

```{r step2_receiver_sender}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Define Receiver and Sender Cell Types
#-----------------------------------------------
# Define the receiver cell type
receiver <- params$receiver

# Define senders: all other cell types in the dataset
# FIX: as.character() - unique(Idents()) is a factor
all_cell_types <- as.character(unique(Idents(seurat_obj)))
sender_celltypes <- all_cell_types[all_cell_types != receiver]
# ADDED: optional explicit sender set (empty = all other cell types, as in the article)
if (nzchar(params$sender.celltypes)) {
  sender_celltypes <- trimws(strsplit(params$sender.celltypes, ",")[[1]])
}
sender_celltypes  # inspect the list

# Define the condition comparison
condition_oi        <- params$condition.oi         # condition of interest
condition_reference <- params$condition.reference  # reference condition

# ADDED: check that receiver, senders and conditions exist in the object
stopifnot(receiver %in% all_cell_types,
          all(sender_celltypes %in% all_cell_types),
          !receiver %in% sender_celltypes,
          all(c(condition_oi, condition_reference) %in% seurat_obj[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]]))
```

## Determine expressed genes in receiver and sender cells

```{r step3_expressed_genes}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Determine Expressed Genes in Receiver and Sender Cells
#-----------------------------------------------
# Extract the count matrix and cell identity vector once for efficiency.
expr_mat    <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, assay = params$assay, layer = "counts")
cell_idents <- Idents(seurat_obj)

# Identify expressed genes in the receiver population
# A gene is "expressed" if detected in >=10% of receiver cells
expressed_genes_receiver <- get_expressed_genes(
  celltype_oi    = receiver,
  object         = expr_mat,
  celltype_annot = cell_idents,
  pct            = params$expressed.pct
)

# Define background genes: expressed receiver genes present in the NicheNet model
background_expressed_genes <- expressed_genes_receiver %>%
  .[. %in% rownames(ligand_target_matrix)]

# Identify expressed genes in each sender cell type (reuse the same matrix/idents)
list_expressed_genes_sender <- sender_celltypes %>%
  lapply(function(ct) get_expressed_genes(
    celltype_oi    = ct,
    object         = expr_mat,
    celltype_annot = cell_idents,
    pct            = params$expressed.pct
  ))

expressed_genes_sender <- list_expressed_genes_sender %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

# ADDED: report the sizes
cat("Expressed genes in receiver:", length(expressed_genes_receiver), "\n")
cat("Background genes (also in the ligand-target matrix):", length(background_expressed_genes), "\n")
cat("Expressed genes in senders (union):", length(expressed_genes_sender), "\n")
```

## Define the gene set of interest

```{r step4_geneset}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Define the Gene Set of Interest
#-----------------------------------------------
# Subset to receiver cell type
seurat_receiver <- subset(seurat_obj, idents = receiver)

# Set condition as identity for DE testing within receiver cells
Idents(seurat_receiver) <- seurat_receiver[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]]

# Find DE genes: Post_Treatment vs Healthy in CD4+ T cells
DE_table_receiver <- FindMarkers(
  object   = seurat_receiver,
  ident.1  = condition_oi,
  ident.2  = condition_reference,
  min.pct  = params$de.min_pct
)

# Filter to significant, biologically meaningful DE genes
# and restrict to genes present in the NicheNet ligand-target model
geneset_oi <- DE_table_receiver %>%
  filter(p_val_adj <= params$de.padj & avg_log2FC >= params$de.log2fc) %>%  # upregulated in Post_Treatment
  rownames() %>%
  intersect(rownames(ligand_target_matrix))

length(geneset_oi)  # how many genes passed filtering? 26 in our case

# ADDED: the ligand activity analysis cannot run on an empty gene set
stopifnot(length(geneset_oi) > 0)
write.csv(DE_table_receiver, file.path(nichenet.dir, "results/DE_table_receiver.csv"))
```

## Define potential ligands

```{r step5_potential_ligands}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Define Potential Ligands
#-----------------------------------------------
# Identify all receptors expressed by the receiver population
expressed_receptors <- intersect(
  lr_network$to,
  expressed_genes_receiver
)

# Format of lr_network
#  from  to    
#  A2M   MMP2  
#  A2M   MMP9  
#  A2M   LRP1  
#  A2M   KLK3  
#  AANAT MTNR1A
#  AANAT MTNR1B

# --- Sender-agnostic approach ---
# Potential ligands: any ligand in the network with an expressed receptor in receiver.
all_genes_detected <- rownames(seurat_obj)

potential_ligands_agnostic <- lr_network %>%
  filter(to %in% expressed_receptors) %>%
  pull(from) %>%
  unique() %>%
  intersect(all_genes_detected)  # keep only ligands present in the assay

# --- Sender-focused approach ---
expressed_ligands_sender <- intersect(
  lr_network$from,
  expressed_genes_sender
)

# Potential ligands: expressed in sender AND have expressed receptor in receiver
potential_ligands_focused <- lr_network %>%
  filter(from %in% expressed_ligands_sender & to %in% expressed_receptors) %>%
  pull(from) %>%
  unique()

# ADDED: report the sizes
cat("Expressed receptors in receiver:", length(expressed_receptors), "\n")
cat("Potential ligands (sender-agnostic):", length(potential_ligands_agnostic), "\n")
cat("Potential ligands (sender-focused):", length(potential_ligands_focused), "\n")
```

## Run ligand activity analysis

```{r step6_ligand_activity}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: Run Ligand Activity Analysis
#-----------------------------------------------
# Run ligand activity analysis — sender-agnostic
ligand_activities_agnostic <- predict_ligand_activities(
  geneset                  = geneset_oi,
  background_expressed_genes = background_expressed_genes,
  ligand_target_matrix     = ligand_target_matrix,
  potential_ligands        = potential_ligands_agnostic
)

# Run ligand activity analysis — sender-focused
ligand_activities_focused <- predict_ligand_activities(
  geneset                  = geneset_oi,
  background_expressed_genes = background_expressed_genes,
  ligand_target_matrix     = ligand_target_matrix,
  potential_ligands        = potential_ligands_focused
)

# Sort by corrected AUPR and assign rank using row_number() on the sorted result.
ligand_activities_agnostic <- ligand_activities_agnostic %>%
  arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number())

ligand_activities_focused <- ligand_activities_focused %>%
  arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number())

# ADDED: show the top of each table and save them
print(head(ligand_activities_agnostic, 10))
print(head(ligand_activities_focused, 10))
write.csv(ligand_activities_agnostic, file.path(nichenet.dir, "results/ligand_activities_agnostic.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ligand_activities_focused, file.path(nichenet.dir, "results/ligand_activities_focused.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Select top ligands for downstream analysis

```{r step7_top_ligands}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: Select Top Ligands for Downstream Analysis
#-----------------------------------------------
# Select top 20 ligands from each approach
top_n <- params$top.n.ligands

best_upstream_ligands_agnostic <- ligand_activities_agnostic %>%
  top_n(top_n, aupr_corrected) %>%
  pull(test_ligand) %>%
  unique()

best_upstream_ligands_focused <- ligand_activities_focused %>%
  top_n(top_n, aupr_corrected) %>%
  pull(test_ligand) %>%
  unique()

# Combine (union of both approaches for comprehensive follow-up)
best_upstream_ligands <- union(
  best_upstream_ligands_agnostic,
  best_upstream_ligands_focused
)

cat("Top ligands (agnostic):", paste(best_upstream_ligands_agnostic, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Top ligands (focused): ", paste(best_upstream_ligands_focused, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Union:", length(best_upstream_ligands), "ligands\n")
```

```{r step7_save}
# lr_network here is the de-duplicated version from Step 1)
saveRDS(seurat_obj, file.path(nichenet.dir, "results/seurat_nichenet_input.rds"))
save(receiver, sender_celltypes, condition_oi, condition_reference, top_n,

     potential_ligands_agnostic, potential_ligands_focused,
     ligand_activities_agnostic, ligand_activities_focused,
     best_upstream_ligands_agnostic, best_upstream_ligands_focused,
     best_upstream_ligands,
     file = file.path(nichenet.dir, "results/nichenet_part1_state.RData"))
```
